transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thanks for seeing me. Um... I came in because, well, for a while now, I've had this feeling—or I guess I'm pretty convinced—that certain people around here in Cincinnati, mostly in the arts and finance circles, are quietly tracking my movements. Like, they know which clients I'm meeting with. And it feels like they're sending me little signals about it. Sometimes it's through the invitations I get, or the topics at panels, or even just who happens to sit near me at networking events. I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, but... I just can't really let it go. It's been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
When you think about people tracking you and sending signals—do you think there's any possibility that this might not actually be happening, or are you completely certain that it is?

I mean, like I mentioned a minute ago, I do try to tell myself that it could just be a coincidence. I know how it sounds. Part of me realizes it might not actually be happening—that maybe these folks in the arts and finance circles aren't really coordinating who sits near me or what the panel topics are just to show they know my client list. 

So, yeah, I guess there is a possibility that I'm wrong. But... I just can't really let it go. Even when I try to rationalize it, the feeling is just so strong that I always end up back to being pretty convinced that it is real.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear any voices or see things that aren't there. It's really just... just the feeling that people are tracking me and sending those signals. But no, no voices or anything visual.

Over the past few weeks or months, have there been times when you felt more convinced about this tracking, and other times when you felt less convinced? Or has your level of certainty stayed pretty much the same?

It's fluctuated a little, I guess. But mostly, it stays pretty consistent. Like I said before, I'll have moments where I try to talk myself down—where I tell myself, "Okay, this is just a coincidence. These people in the arts and finance scenes aren't actually tracking my client meetings or sending me messages through panel topics or seating arrangements." 

During those moments, I might feel a little less convinced. But it never lasts long. I always end up right back where I started, feeling just as certain that they are doing it. So even when I try to brush it off, I just can't let it go. The feeling that they're tracking me is just always there, hovering in the background.

When you think about this tracking situation, have your ideas about it become more detailed or complex over time? For example, have you started to figure out more about how they're doing it, or who specifically is involved, or what their overall plan or motive might be?

No, not really. It hasn't really grown into some big, complicated theory or anything. I mean, I don't know exactly how they're pulling it off, or what their ultimate motive even is. 

I haven't figured out a specific master plan. It's really just the same stuff I've been noticing all along—the seating arrangements, the topics they choose to talk about when I'm around. It hasn't gotten more detailed or deeper over time, it just... it just stays exactly what it is. I just know what I'm seeing, but I don't have all the answers for the why or the how.

When did you first start noticing this feeling that people were tracking you? And since it started, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your work, maintain relationships, or take care of daily things like sleep or hygiene?

I'd say it's been going on for about two months now. That's when I first started noticing that people were tracking my client meetings and... and sending me those signals. 

As far as my work or my daily routine goes, I haven't really noticed any major changes. I'm still doing my job, and I'm keeping up with things like sleep and taking care of myself just fine. It's really just that this whole situation with the tracking has been happening for the past couple of months.

If someone you trusted completely—like a close friend or family member—looked into this situation and told you they found no evidence that people were actually tracking you, would that be enough to make you seriously question whether it's really happening, or would you still feel convinced that it is?

I think... I mean, if someone I really trusted told me that, I might pause for a second. I might try to tell myself again that it's just a coincidence. But honestly? I'd probably still feel convinced it's happening. 

Like I said, I've been dealing with this for a while—feeling like these people in the arts and finance circles in Cincinnati are tracking my client meetings. And even when I try to talk myself out of it, or think about how it might just be the invitations, the panel topics, or who sits near me at events... I just can't really let it go. So, yeah, even if a friend told me they didn't see it, I don't think it would change my mind. The feeling is just too real for me to ignore.

When you really think about it deeply, is there any part of you that genuinely believes this tracking might not be happening, or do you think that deep down you're actually certain it's real even though you say you try to doubt it?

I mean... deep down, I think I'm certain it's real. I know I said I try to tell myself it's just a coincidence, but... I can't actually make myself believe that. 

When I look at it all—the invitations, the panel topics, the way those people from the arts and finance circles always seem to sit right near me at events... it's just too specific. They know which clients I'm meeting with, and they're sending me those little signals about it. So, yeah, even when I try to doubt it, I just can't let it go. I really do believe it's happening.
